title: The Rhine Alpine Triangle, Vaduz, the Silvretta and Graubünden
subRegion: Alpine Rhine valley, Vorarlberg and Graubünden

bestPeriod.note: The Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse and Furkajoch open in June and close in late October; everything below 1,700 m works from May.

summary: One base in Vaduz, six day loops into three countries, the Silvretta, the Bregenzerwald, the Ruinaulta gorge and the Graubünden passes.
hook: Liechtenstein is 25 km long and has one mountain road. That is not a limitation here, it is the reason the trip works. From a single base in Vaduz you can be on an Austrian toll pass at 2,032 m or above a Swiss river gorge within ninety minutes, and be back for dinner in a country with no motorway at all.

snapshot.Country: Liechtenstein (with Austria and Switzerland day loops)
snapshot.Base(s): Vaduz, 6 nights; one optional night in Malbun
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 1,230 km; valley motorway plus alpine passes, gradients to 12%, max altitude 2,032 m
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Zürich (ZRH), 120 km; Friedrichshafen (FDH) and Innsbruck (INN) are alternatives
snapshot.Who It Suits: Drivers who prefer one unpacked suitcase and six different countries' worth of road

itinerary.title: Zürich to the Fürstentum
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Zürich airport. A Swiss-registered rental almost always carries the **Autobahnvignette** already; check the windscreen or, for the e-vignette, that your plate is registered. Take the A3 along the Zürichsee and the Walensee, an hour of lake and limestone wall.
itinerary.afternoon: Leave the motorway at Sargans, cross the Rhine at Trübbach and enter Liechtenstein. No border post, no formalities, no Liechtenstein road charge, the country has no motorway to charge for. Settle in Vaduz, 455 m.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Städtle: the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein and Hilti Art Foundation share a black basalt cube, the Landesmuseum is opposite, and the castle sits on its rock above, closed to visitors but photogenic from the vineyard path. Park in the underground Städtle garage; surface bays are short-stay blue-zone.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km · 1h30 driving · no passes · max altitude 455 m.

itinerary.title: The one mountain road
itinerary.morning: Drive Liechtenstein's only alpine road: Vaduz to **Triesenberg** (884 m) on tight switchbacks with a 10% average, then through the Gnalp-Steg tunnel to **Steg** (1,300 m) and up to **Malbun** at 1,600 m. Fifteen kilometres, 1,150 m of climb, and a dead end, Malbun has no through route to anywhere.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the Sareis chairlift to 2,000 m for the ridge view into Austria, then drive down and south to **Balzers**, where Burg Gutenberg stands on a free-standing knoll above the Rhine.
itinerary.evening: Back in Vaduz, book a tasting at the **Hofkellerei des Fürsten von Liechtenstein**, the princely wine estate on the slope below the castle. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, and a short walk from the Städtle.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km · 1h30 driving · 1 climb (Malbun, dead end) · max altitude 1,600 m.

itinerary.title: Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse
itinerary.morning: North into Austria via Feldkirch. You need the **Austrian digital Vignette** for the A14 Rheintalautobahn and the S16, around €13 for ten days, bought from the ASFINAG app, valid immediately. Run the Walgau to Bludenz, then over the **Arlbergpass**, 1,793 m, on the free B197 rather than the tolled S16 tunnel, into Landeck.
itinerary.afternoon: South up the Paznaun through Ischgl to Galtür for the **Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse**: 34 hairpins, gradients to 12%. The lower Partenen ramp on the Vorarlberg side is shut for rockfall barrier works until summer 2030, so in 2026 the road is driven as a toll-free there-and-back from Galtür (open from 4 June) as far as the Vermuntsee. The **Bielerhöhe** at 2,032 m sits on the dam wall of the Silvretta-Stausee, with the Piz Buin behind it and a large car park that is the only easy parking on the whole road.
itinerary.evening: Retrace through Ischgl and Landeck, back over the Arlbergpass and down the Klostertal to Bludenz and home.
itinerary.dayStats: 230 km · 4h15 driving · 2 passes (Arlbergpass, Bielerhöhe) · max altitude 2,032 m.

itinerary.title: Furkajoch and the Bregenzerwald
itinerary.morning: Feldkirch, then Rankweil and up the Laternsertal to the **Furkajoch**, 1,761 m, a narrow, unfenced Vorarlberg pass, closed from November to May, with passing places rather than two full lanes. Not for wide vehicles. Over to **Damüls**, one of the highest villages in the region.
itinerary.afternoon: Down the **Faschinajoch** (1,486 m) or straight on to Au and the Bregenzerwald proper: Schwarzenberg, Bezau and Andelsbuch, where contemporary timber architecture sits next to 300-year-old farmhouses. The Werkraum Bregenzerwald in Andelsbuch shows what the local joiners actually make.
itinerary.evening: Over the **Bödele** (1,140 m) to Dornbirn, then Bregenz for the Bodensee at dusk. Back to Vaduz on the A14.
itinerary.dayStats: 210 km · 4h00 driving · 3 passes (Furkajoch, Faschinajoch, Bödele) · max altitude 1,761 m.

itinerary.title: Ruinaulta and the Viamala
itinerary.morning: South on the Swiss A13 to Chur, then up to **Flims**. Park at Flims Waldhaus and walk 40 minutes to **Conn** and the **Il Spir** viewing platform, a cantilevered timber spiral hanging over the **Ruinaulta**, the Rhine gorge cut through the debris of a prehistoric landslide.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive the gorge's southern rim through Ilanz and down the hairpins to **Versam-Safien**, then out at Bonaduz. Stop at **Reichenau**, where the Vorderrhein and Hinterrhein meet under a covered bridge and become the Rhine.
itinerary.evening: Continue to Thusis for the **Viamala** gorge, 359 steps down between walls 300 m high on the old road to Italy. Return north on the A13. If you have time and light, the **San Bernardino** pass at 2,065 m is another 40 minutes south and worth the detour.
itinerary.dayStats: 210 km · 3h40 driving · no passes on the core loop · max altitude 1,100 m.

itinerary.title: Prättigau, Wolfgangpass and Davos
itinerary.morning: A13 to Landquart and up the **Prättigau** through Schiers and Klosters, a long, steady valley climb with the Silvretta chain on the left.
itinerary.afternoon: Over the **Wolfgangpass**, 1,633 m, one of the few Graubünden passes open all year, past the Davosersee into **Davos** at 1,560 m, Europe's highest town of its size. Continue over the **Flüelapass** (2,383 m) only if it is open; it is a summer road, closed roughly November to May, and the Vereina car-train through the mountain is the winter alternative.
itinerary.evening: Loop back via Filisur and the **Lenzerheide** (1,549 m) to Chur, then the Rhine valley home. Detour to see the Landwasser viaduct near Filisur if the light holds.
itinerary.dayStats: 235 km · 4h10 driving · 2 passes (Wolfgangpass, Lenzerheide) · max altitude 1,633 m.

itinerary.title: Rhine valley and out
itinerary.morning: Cross to **Werdenberg** at Buchs, a lakeside cluster of medieval timber houses below a castle, then **Bad Ragaz** and the **Taminaschlucht**, the gorge where the thermal spring emerges. The last kilometre to the old baths is closed to private cars; a shuttle runs from the valley station.
itinerary.afternoon: North on the A3 along the Walensee to Zürich. Refuel in Liechtenstein or Austria before leaving; Swiss fuel is the most expensive of the three.
itinerary.evening: Drop the car at Zürich airport. Swiss returns want a full tank and heavy refuelling surcharges if not.
itinerary.dayStats: 145 km · 2h00 driving · no passes · max altitude 520 m.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Gasthof Löwen
accommodationStrategy.description: A 14th-century timber-framed house on the main road through Vaduz, with parking and a walkable position between the Städtle and the vineyards. Six nights in one bed is the whole logic of this trip, and the Löwen puts you five minutes from the motorway ramp at Trübbach.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months in summer; Liechtenstein has under 1,000 hotel beds in total.

accommodationStrategy.name: Park Hotel Sonnenhof
accommodationStrategy.description: Above the town on the slope below the castle, with its own garden, indoor parking and a view straight down the Rhine valley to the Swiss peaks. Worth it for the last two nights if you want the driving days bracketed by something restorative.

accommodationStrategy.name: Gorfion Familotel
accommodationStrategy.description: If you want one night at altitude, Malbun at 1,600 m is the only option in the country, and the Gorfion is built for families with outdoor parking and ski-and-hike storage. Waking above the tunnel means the Sareis lift and the ridge paths before anyone drives up from the valley.

logistics.emergency: 112 everywhere. In Liechtenstein and Switzerland: police 117, fire 118, ambulance 144, and **Rega air rescue on 1414**. Austrian alpine rescue is 140.
logistics.money: Liechtenstein uses the Swiss franc and is inside the Swiss customs union, but euros are accepted at many Vaduz counters at an unfavourable rate. Card everywhere; Austrian Gasthäuser still like cash.

other.label: Three road-charge regimes in one week
other.text: Liechtenstein has no motorway and charges nothing. Switzerland requires the **Autobahnvignette** at CHF 40 (approx. €42), annual only, no short-term option, valid 1 December to 31 January of the following year, now available as a plate-linked e-vignette. Austria requires its own **digital Vignette** for Autobahnen and Schnellstrassen, from about €13 for ten days. Neither covers the other, and neither covers special tolls.

other.label: Special tolls are extra
other.text: The S16 Arlberg road tunnel (approx. €12.50) is charged at its own barrier on top of the Austrian Vignette; the Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse is toll-free while its Vorarlberg side remains shut for construction. The Swiss vignette likewise does not cover the Vereina or Furka car-trains.

other.label: Rentals and cross-border
other.text: There is no meaningful car hire in Liechtenstein itself, rent in Zürich, St. Gallen-Altenrhein or Friedrichshafen. Swiss rentals include the Swiss vignette but not the Austrian one; Austrian and German rentals are the reverse. Cross-border into CH/AT/DE/IT/LI is standard on all three; one-way drops between countries typically run €150, €400.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 everywhere. In Liechtenstein and Switzerland: police 117, fire 118, ambulance 144, and **Rega air rescue on 1414**. Austrian alpine rescue is 140.

other.label: Driving rules differ by border
other.text: Switzerland and Liechtenstein require dipped headlights in daylight; Austria does not. Swiss speeding fines are income-scaled and severe, and the A13 Rhine valley is heavily camera-monitored. Alcohol limits are 0.5‰ in all three.

other.label: Fuel
other.text: Cheapest in Austria (Feldkirch, Bludenz), then Liechtenstein, then Switzerland. Fill in Vorarlberg on the Silvretta and Bregenzerwald days.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Alpine pass roads with gates, Silvretta above all, close overnight. Swiss shops shut at 18:30 and all Sunday; Liechtenstein observes its own national holiday on 15 August, when almost everything closes.

proTips: Get your Liechtenstein passport stamp at the Vaduz tourist office in the Städtle for a couple of francs. It is a souvenir stamp, not a border control, and it is the only one in the country.
Fill the tank at Feldkirch on the way home from Austria every time. Over six days the saving against Swiss prices covers a pass toll.
Drive the Furkajoch eastbound in the morning: the west ramp is the narrow one, and meeting a coach on it downhill is the day's worst moment.
Buy the Austrian ten-day Vignette from the ASFINAG app rather than a reseller, it activates the moment you pay, with no statutory waiting period.
Walk to Il Spir from Flims Waldhaus rather than driving to Conn. The upper road is restricted to residents and buses, and the walk is the flat 40 minutes through the forest.
The Bielerhöhe car park is the only comfortable stop on the Silvretta road. Everything else is a widened bend with room for three cars.
Check the Graubünden pass status page before the Davos day. Flüela and Albula can be closed while Wolfgang and Julier are open, which changes the loop entirely.

packingNotes: Swiss francs in cash, roughly CHF 200, plus €100 for Austrian tolls and Gasthäuser.
A windproof layer for Sareis at 2,000 m and the Bielerhöhe dam wall, which is exposed in any weather.
Walking shoes for Il Spir, the Viamala steps and the Taminaschlucht, all wet stone.
Sunglasses and screen cleaner; the Rhine valley runs into low sun morning and evening.
Offline maps for Vorarlberg's side valleys, where signal drops out completely.
A small daypack, every loop involves at least one 40-minute walk from a car park.
Swimwear for the Bad Ragaz thermal baths on the last morning.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The Furkajoch is still closed in June, or the Silvretta's Galtür approach is shut by snow.** Fallback: run the Arlberg, Flexenpass (1,773 m) and Hochtannbergpass (1,676 m) loop through Lech and the Bregenzerwald instead, all lower, all open earlier.

**You cross into Austria without the Austrian Vignette.** Cameras on the A14 catch it immediately and the on-the-spot substitute toll is far more than the vignette. Fallback: buy it on the app before Feldkirch, or stay on the free B190/B191 valley roads.

**Weather closes the Vaduz-Malbun road.** It is the country's only mountain road and there is no alternative route. Fallback: Malbun's post buses keep running with chains when private cars are turned back.

**Zürich airport drop-off timing.** The A3 through Pfäffikon backs up badly on Sunday evenings and Friday afternoons. Fallback: allow 2h15 rather than 1h30, or route via the A13 and A1 through St. Gallen.
